tasks.short: Key supplier and customer invoices into AFAS, post them, and pull reports from the ledger.

today.trigger: Invoices arrive by email, Peppol/UBL or post; customer orders are ready to bill.
steps: Open the invoice PDF or UBL file from the AP mailbox
Find the supplier in AFAS and check its details
Key or correct the header and lines, then post
Send the invoice for approval by email or in AFAS
Export lists to Excel for questions and month close
drudgery: Retyping PDF invoices that are not UBL
Rebuilding the same Excel exports every week
today.time_sinks: PDF invoices without UBL and the approval round, which a Dutch survey says is still paper or email for 70% of companies.

lenses.faster: UBL invoices and one-to-one matches with an order or receipt post and approve themselves in AFAS; the bookkeeper only opens the misses.
lenses.autonomous: Each incoming invoice triggers scan and recognise, supplier lookup by KvK, VAT number and IBAN, matching and posting without a reminder.
lenses.ambitious: Every supplier sends UBL and every invoice is in AFAS the day it arrives, ready for the 2030 e-invoicing duty and the 5-day reporting of intra-EU purchases.
lenses.joy: No more retyping; the work left is fixing supplier data and odd invoices, which needs judgement.
lenses.options: Test several match tolerances on last quarter's invoices and pick the one with most touchless postings and no wrong ones.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the match rules, tolerances and supplier master data instead of keying invoices.
reach: Maintain supplier master data checks with the Controller

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which supplier, site or order an odd invoice really belongs to, and deciding when a rule should change.
tasks.pattern_why: UBL fields and order/receipt matching are structured and checkable; AFAS already does it with rules. PDF capture is a separate llm_step feeding the same flow.

in_practice.trigger: Invoice lands in the AP mailbox or Peppol inbox.
steps: AFAS scan and recognise turns the PDF into an e-invoice or reads the UBL
Supplier found by KvK, VAT number and IBAN
Match against purchase order or goods receipt within set tolerance
Matched invoices post and go to payment; misses go to the bookkeeper's queue
Weekly report of touchless share and miss reasons
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper handles every unmatched or new-supplier invoice; Controller signs off tolerance changes.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS workflow history per invoice, plus a touchless-share dashboard in Power BI.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 reads UBL and PDF invoices to line level and posts and approves one-to-one matches.
AFAS scan and recognise finds the supplier by KvK, VAT number and IBAN; gaps are filled by hand.
Escalante Golf cut invoice handling from 2.5 minutes to 45 seconds per invoice.
70% of Dutch respondents still approve invoices on paper or by email.
evidence.source: Accountancy Vanmorgen / Wolters Kluwer survey, 8 Sep 2026

risks: Touchless share stays low because many purchases have no order in AFAS
Wrong supplier match on shared IBANs or group companies
A loose tolerance posts overcharges without anyone seeing them
research_questions: What share of last year's invoices had a purchase order or goods receipt in AFAS?
How many suppliers can send UBL today, and how many of the top 50 by volume?
What touchless share does AFAS reach on a month of Noordhaven invoices in a test environment?

tasks.short: Check postings for wrong amounts, VAT codes, ledger accounts and cost centres before they count.

today.trigger: Daily batch of posted invoices and journals; pre-close review.
steps: Scan posted entries in AFAS lists
Recalculate VAT and totals on doubtful invoices
Check ledger account and cost centre against the supplier's usual coding
Correct entries and note why
Fix what the Controller or auditor flags at close
drudgery: Fixing the same supplier's coding error every month
today.time_sinks: Manual review of every line because nobody knows where the errors are.

lenses.faster: Rule checks flag VAT mismatches, unusual accounts, duplicate invoice numbers and sums that do not add up; the bookkeeper only reviews flags.
lenses.autonomous: Checks run on every posting overnight and the list is ready in the morning.
lenses.ambitious: Every entry checked, not a sample, so audit adjustments drop and close is faster.
lenses.joy: No more scanning lists; the work becomes finding why an error happens and stopping it at the source.
lenses.options: An LLM explains each flag in plain language with two or three likely fixes.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper designs and tunes the check rules and tracks which ones catch real errors.
reach: Pre-close review normally done by the Accountant
Audit preparation lists for the Controller

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether an unusual entry is wrong or just unusual, and talking to the person who coded it.
tasks.pattern_why: Arithmetic, VAT code and account checks are rules on structured AFAS data; an llm_step can add a plain-language explanation of flags.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly after the AFAS extract refresh.
steps: Run rule checks: VAT rate vs code, totals, duplicates, account vs supplier history
Score and rank flags
LLM writes a one-line explanation per flag
Bookkeeper corrects or dismisses each flag with a reason
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper decides on every correction; dismissed flags feed rule tuning.
data_needed: Posted entries with VAT codes and accounts
in_practice.logs_to: Flag log with decision and reason, kept for the auditor.

evidence.claim: Coding suggested from vendor history is reviewed and confirmed by staff for accountability.
Own ledger accounts, VAT codes and exceptions per administration block full automation.
evidence.source: Accountancy Vanmorgen, Zenvoices branded content, 2 Jul 2026

evidence.claim: Rule-based anomaly checks on ledger data are standard in finance tooling.

risks: Too many false flags and people stop reading them
Checks miss errors the rules were not written for
research_questions: How many audit adjustments last year came from coding or VAT errors?
Which ten rules would have caught most corrections made in the last six months?
What false-flag rate is acceptable to the team?

tasks.short: Pick ledger account, cost centre, site and VAT code for each invoice or receipt.

today.trigger: Invoice without a matching order, or a receipt or expense claim comes in.
steps: Read the invoice to see what was bought and for which site
Look up how this supplier was coded last time
Choose account, cost centre (Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo) and VAT code
Ask the budget holder when unclear
drudgery: Looking up last month's coding for the same supplier
Emailing sites about which cost centre to use
today.time_sinks: Non-order invoices and mixed invoices covering several sites.

lenses.faster: A coding suggestion from supplier history and invoice text arrives with each invoice; the bookkeeper accepts or changes it.
lenses.autonomous: Suppliers with stable coding history get coded automatically; new or mixed invoices wait for a person.
lenses.ambitious: Consistent coding per site and cost type, so Power BI cost reports are trusted without manual reclassing at close.
lenses.joy: No more lookups; what is left is the genuinely unclear invoices.
lenses.options: Show the top three coding options with their history share instead of one guess.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the chart of accounts mapping and coding procedures that the suggestions learn from.
reach: Cost allocation reclasses the Accountant does at close
Feedback to FP&A on cost categories

tasks.human_edge: Knowing what was actually bought and for which site when the invoice text is vague.
tasks.pattern_why: Invoice text is unstructured; the output (account, cost centre, VAT code) is structured and checkable against history and rules.

in_practice.trigger: Invoice recognised in AFAS without a purchase order match.
steps: Read invoice text and supplier history
Suggest account, cost centre and VAT code with confidence
Auto-apply above a confidence threshold for known suppliers
Queue the rest for the bookkeeper
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper accepts or changes each suggestion below the threshold; monthly sample of auto-coded invoices.
data_needed: Chart of accounts and cost centres
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS invoice history with suggestion, final coding and who changed it.

evidence.claim: Invoice coding suggested from vendor history for teams to review and confirm.
A booking proposal is digitising, not automating; measured touchless shares disappoint.
evidence.source: Accountancy Vanmorgen, Zenvoices branded content, 2 Jul 2026

risks: Bookkeepers accept suggestions without reading them
research_questions: How stable is coding per supplier in the last 12 months?
What share of invoices are non-order or multi-site?
Does AFAS's booking proposal reach the accuracy needed, or is an extra model required?

tasks.short: Work out amounts due, late-payment interest, credit notes, discounts and open balances.

today.trigger: Billing run, a dispute, a supplier statement or a late customer.
steps: Pull open items from AFAS
Calculate interest, discounts or partial payments in Excel
Check against contract terms or price agreements
Post the result or send it to the customer or supplier
drudgery: Looking up payment terms in contracts
today.time_sinks: One-off spreadsheets for each dispute or statement.

lenses.faster: Interest, discounts and balances calculated in AFAS or a small tool from terms stored per customer and supplier.
lenses.autonomous: Statutory commercial interest and agreed discounts calculate themselves on every overdue item.
lenses.ambitious: Terms checked against the law: Noordhaven as a large company may not agree more than 30 days with small suppliers.
lenses.joy: No more spreadsheet arithmetic; time goes to disputes that need a conversation.
lenses.options: Show the customer three settlement scenarios (pay now, instalments, with or without interest waived).
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains the term and rate tables the calculations use.
reach: Interest and settlement proposals for the Credit and Collections Officer

tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether to charge or waive interest for a valued customer.
tasks.pattern_why: The formulas and rates are fixed and written down; outputs are exact and checkable.

in_practice.trigger: Item passes due date, or a statement or dispute is logged.
steps: Read terms and rate tables
Calculate interest, discount or balance
Flag terms longer than 30 days with small suppliers
Post or propose, depending on amount
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves waivers and settlements; Controller above a set amount.
data_needed: Payment terms per customer and supplier
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS memo on the item with calculation basis.

evidence.claim: BW 6:119a limits payment terms a large company may agree with a small supplier to 30 days.
Billing, interest and account status can run as rules with autonomy 4.

risks: Wrong term data gives wrong interest at scale
Charging interest damages customer relations without context
research_questions: How complete are payment terms per customer and supplier in AFAS?
How many supplier contracts exceed 30 days with small suppliers?
Does Noordhaven want to charge statutory interest at all?

tasks.short: Prepare payment runs for suppliers, flex agencies, VAT and wage tax, and send batches to Rabobank.

today.trigger: Weekly payment run and tax deadlines.
steps: Select due and approved invoices in AFAS
Check IBAN changes and possible duplicates
Split agency invoices into the g-rekening part and the rest
Create the SEPA batch and upload to Rabobank
Get the second signature from the Controller or Finance Director
drudgery: Calculating the g-rekening split per agency invoice
today.time_sinks: Pre-run checks and agency invoice splits.

lenses.faster: AFAS builds the run; checks for IBAN changes, duplicates and the g-rekening split run before the batch is shown.
lenses.autonomous: The proposal is ready every Tuesday with flags; nobody has to start it.
lenses.ambitious: Pay small suppliers on time, keep the g-rekening split complete to limit inlenersaansprakelijkheid, and catch fraud attempts every time.
lenses.joy: No hunting for duplicates; the bookkeeper looks at flags and signs.
lenses.options: Show cash scenarios: pay all, pay by due date, or hold large items until receipts come in.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the run rules, fraud checks and the agency split logic.
reach: Short-term cash view for the FP&A Analyst
Agency liability file for the Controller

tasks.human_edge: Approving money leaving the company and calling a supplier when an IBAN change looks odd.
tasks.pattern_why: Selection, split and checks are rules; the run needs a human approval because payments are hard to reverse.

in_practice.trigger: Scheduled weekly run and tax due dates.
steps: Select approved due items
Check IBAN changes, duplicates and Rabobank name-check warnings
Split agency invoices to g-rekening share
Present the batch with flags for approval
Upload to Rabobank after dual signature
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper reviews flags; dual signature in Rabobank for every batch.
data_needed: Agency wage-cost shares and payment-behaviour statements
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS payment run history and Rabobank batch log.

evidence.claim: Noordhaven can be held liable for agencies' unpaid wage tax and VAT and limits this by paying into the g-rekening.
Since October 2025 banks check payee name against IBAN; a payer who confirms after a warning is not blocked.
Cheques are rare in Dutch practice.

risks: Wrong g-rekening share leaves liability open
research_questions: What is the correct wage-cost share per agency and is it on each invoice?
How many IBAN changes per month, and how are they verified today?
Can AFAS hold the g-rekening split natively?

tasks.short: Reconcile bank, agency hours and subledgers against the general ledger and clear differences.

today.trigger: Daily bank statements; monthly close; agency invoices.
steps: Import CAMT.053 statements into AFAS
Match unmatched lines by hand
Compare agency invoices with hours in the portals and timesheets
Reconcile AP and AR subledgers to the ledger in Excel
Explain remaining differences to the Controller
drudgery: Matching bank lines one by one
Comparing agency hours line by line
today.time_sinks: Unmatched bank lines and agency invoice checks with 150 to 300 flex workers.

lenses.faster: AFAS rules match bank lines; a script compares agency invoices with recorded hours; only differences reach a person.
lenses.autonomous: Matching runs on each statement import and each agency invoice.
lenses.ambitious: Every agency hour checked against site time records, not a sample.
lenses.joy: No line-by-line ticking; the work left is the real differences.
lenses.options: An LLM proposes likely matches for unmatched lines with reasons.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper tunes match rules and tolerances.
reach: Flex labour cost reporting for HR and FP&A
Balance sheet reconciliations of the Accountant

tasks.human_edge: Calling an agency or site about a disputed hour.
tasks.pattern_why: Matching on reference, IBAN, invoice number and hours is rule-based; an llm_step explains leftovers.

in_practice.trigger: Statement import or agency invoice received.
steps: AFAS matches bank lines on reference, IBAN, invoice number, then oldest-first sums
Compare agency invoice lines with hours from site records
LLM suggests explanations for unmatched items
Bookkeeper resolves differences
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper decides on every unmatched line and agency difference.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS match history and a difference log per agency.

evidence.claim: AFAS matches CAMT.053 lines on payment reference, IBAN, invoice number, then oldest-first sums; misses go to a person.
Comparing agency invoices with time records is rule-based reconciliation.

risks: Agency portals cannot export hours cleanly
Loose tolerances hide small but repeated overbilling
research_questions: Can each of the three agencies export hours in a structured format?
What share of bank lines does AFAS match automatically today?
How much did agency differences amount to last year?

tasks.short: Answer supplier, customer and colleague questions about invoices, payments and balances.

today.trigger: Email or phone question in the AP/AR mailbox.
steps: Read the question
Look up the invoice or payment in AFAS
Check approval status or payment date
Reply by email
drudgery: Answering 'when do I get paid?' many times a day
Searching for invoices by unclear references

lenses.faster: An agent reads the email, looks up the status in AFAS and drafts the reply.
lenses.autonomous: Simple status questions get drafted on arrival.
lenses.joy: Fewer repeat questions; the bookkeeper handles complex cases.
lenses.options: Draft replies in Dutch or English, short or detailed.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains reply templates and escalation rules.
reach: First-line customer balance questions for Credit and Collections

tasks.human_edge: Handling an angry supplier or a dispute that needs judgement.
tasks.pattern_why: Several steps and tools with exceptions; replies go out externally so a person approves.

in_practice.trigger: New email in the AP/AR mailbox.
steps: Classify question
Find invoice in AFAS by number, amount or IBAN
Draft reply with status and expected payment date
Bookkeeper approves and sends
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves each reply before sending.
in_practice.logs_to: Outlook sent items and AFAS dossier.

evidence.claim: Payment-status questions answered from AFAS as agent_with_gate, autonomy 3.
Log every AI decision with its data.

risks: Wrong status sent to a supplier
Personal data in emails processed outside AVG/GDPR rules
research_questions: How many status questions per week arrive in the mailbox?
What share can be answered from AFAS data alone?
Do supplier emails contain personal data that needs a DPIA?

tasks.short: Watch open receivables, payables and lease or loan payments so nothing is late.

today.trigger: Weekly ageing review and month close.
steps: Run ageing lists in AFAS
Check overdue items and reasons
Send reminders or pass to Credit and Collections
Check lease and loan instalments against schedules

lenses.faster: Ageing and alerts come from AFAS; reminders go out on schedule.
lenses.autonomous: Reminder runs and alerts trigger by due date.
lenses.ambitious: DSO watched daily per customer, not monthly.
lenses.joy: No list building; focus on customers who need a call.
lenses.options: Rank customers by risk to choose who to call first.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper sets alert thresholds and reminder steps.
reach: First reminder stage for the Credit and Collections Officer

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which customer to call and how.
tasks.pattern_why: Due dates, balances and reminder steps are structured rules.

in_practice.trigger: Daily after the nightly AFAS refresh.
steps: Compute ageing per customer and supplier
Send first reminders automatically
Alert on missed instalments
Escalate to Credit and Collections
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper reviews escalations and holds reminders for disputed items.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS reminder history and Power BI ageing dashboard.

evidence.claim: Billing, interest and account status run as rules with autonomy 4.

research_questions: What is current DSO per site?
How many reminders are sent manually per month?
Are lease schedules stored in AFAS?

role.altitude: From keying, checking and matching invoices to owning the AP/AR system: match rules, tolerances, coding rules, supplier master data and payment controls.
reach: First-line collections for the Credit and Collections Officer
Bank and subledger reconciliations for the Accountant
Flex worker cost and liability checks with HR and the Controller
Cash and DSO inputs for FP&A
role.ceiling_note: Limited by the share of invoices with a purchase order or UBL, the quality of supplier data, agency hour exports, and the need for human approval on payments and external replies.
skills_to_grow: Designing and testing match rules and tolerances in AFAS
Supplier master data governance and fraud checks
role.ambitious_version: A three-person team that runs AP/AR for 1,200 staff with most invoices touchless, every agency hour checked, every supplier paid on time, and month close shortened by days.
